title: Unit 2: Health and Fitness - Key Vocabulary & Grammar
content:
📌 Career (Noun)
• English: An occupation undertaken for a significant period of a person's life with opportunities for progress.
• Amharic: የሥራ መስመር / ሙያዊ ጉዞ
• Synonyms: Profession, Occupation
• Antonyms: Hobby, Pastime
• Example: Zinedine Zidane had an outstanding career as a professional football player.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Profession (Noun)
• English: A paid occupation, especially one that involves prolonged training and a formal qualification.
• Amharic: ሙያ
• Synonyms: Vocation, Career
• Antonyms: Avocation, Hobby
• Example: Teaching is a respected profession that requires continuous learning.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Professional (Adjective / Noun)
• English: Relating to or belonging to a profession; engaged in a specified activity as one's main paid occupation.
• Amharic: ባለሙያ / ፕሮፌሽናል
• Synonyms: Expert, Experienced
• Antonyms: Amateur, Unskilled
• Example: He became a professional athlete after winning the national championship.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Achievements (Noun)
• English: Things done successfully, typically by effort, courage, or skill.
• Amharic: ስኬቶች / የሥራ ውጤቶች
• Synonyms: Accomplishments, Successes
• Antonyms: Failures, Defeats
• Example: Breaking the world record was one of her greatest athletic achievements.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Crowd (Noun)
• English: A large number of people gathered together in a disorganized or crowded way.
• Amharic: የሰዎች ስብስብ / ህዝብ
• Synonyms: Gathering, Multitude, Assembly
• Antonyms: Individual, Isolation
• Example: The football player waved to the cheering crowd in the stadium.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Jog (Verb / Noun)
• English: Run at a steady, gentle pace, especially as a form of physical exercise.
• Amharic: ቀስ ብሎ መሮጥ (ለአካል ብቃት እንቅስቃሴ)
• Synonyms: Trot, Run slowly
• Antonyms: Sprint, Dash
• Example: I usually jog in the park every morning to maintain good fitness.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Assimilate (Verb)
• English: Take in and fully understand information or ideas.
• Amharic: መቀበል፣ መረዳት፣ መዋሃድ
• Synonyms: Absorb, Comprehend
• Antonyms: Misunderstand, Reject
• Example: Reading texts about health helps students assimilate beneficial habits.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Zero Conditional (Grammar Structure)
• English: Used for facts, general truths, and habits (If + Present Simple, Present Simple).
• Amharic: እውነተኛ ነገሮችን እና ልምዶችን ለመግለጽ የሚጠቅም የሰዋሰው ሕግ
• Synonyms: General Truths, Scientific Facts
• Antonyms: Unreal Conditions
• Example: If you exercise regularly, your health improves.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 First Conditional (Grammar Structure)
• English: Used for real and possible situations in the present or future (If + Present Simple, Will + Verb).
• Amharic: ወደፊት ሊሆኑ የሚችሉና እውነተኛ ሁኔታዎችን ለመግለጽ የሚጠቅም
• Synonyms: Real Future Possibility
• Antonyms: Impossible Past Conditions
• Example: If I don't finish my assignment tonight, I will get a low score.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Second Conditional (Grammar Structure)
• English: Used for hypothetical or improbable situations in the present or future (If + Past Simple, Would + Verb).
• Amharic: አሁን ወይም ወደፊት ሊሆኑ የማይችሉ ምናባዊ ሁኔታዎችን ለመግለጽ የሚጠቅም
• Synonyms: Hypothetical Condition, Unreal Present
• Antonyms: Factual Statement
• Example: If I met Zinedine Zidane, I would ask for his autograph.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Third Conditional (Grammar Structure)
• English: Used for imaginary past situations that didn't happen (If + Past Perfect, Would Have + Past Participle).
• Amharic: ባለፈው ጊዜ ያልተከሰቱ ግን ቢሆኑ ኖሮ ተብለው የሚታሰቡ ሁኔታዎችን ለመግለጽ
• Synonyms: Past Regrets, Imaginary Past
• Antonyms: Real Past Events
• Example: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
